To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amino terminus of presenilin 4 (PS4) (residues PS2 1-87) is sufficient for interaction with amyloid precursor protein (APP) and can displace the interaction between PS1 and APP.

(i) the hydrophilic N-terminus of PS2 is sufficient for APP binding, (ii) this region of PS2 is secreted, (iii) the C-terminal region of APP (residues L-100 to L-145) is sufficient for PS2 binding, and (iv) the N-terminal domain of PS2 can compete with PS1/APP binding.

the hydrophilicity of the amino terminus of presenilin is essential for its interaction with amyloid precursor protein and that a region in the extracytoplasmic domain of APP also interacts with presenilin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of the presenilin proteins with the amyloid precursor protein (APP) in order to elucidate the role of presenilions in the processing and secretion of APP.
the molecular basis of the interaction of APP with presenilins.
the identification of the APP/PS interaction domains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PS1 and PS2 bind to the extracellular domain (ECD) of APP and that this interaction is mediated by the hydrophilic N terminus of PS and the ECD of APP.
the interaction between APP and PS2 is mediated by the hydrophilic N-terminal domain of PS2, which can be secreted and can displace PS1/APP complex.
presenilins interact with APP, and that the amino terminus of the presenilin is sufficient for this interaction, and that the A beta region of APP is involved in this interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the amino terminus of presenilin  2 (residules 1-87) is sufficient to interact with the last 45 residues of APP and that this interaction is inhibited by the secretion leader peptide (residules M-1 to 21) of presenilin2.
the hydrophilicity of the N-terminus of presenilns and its leader peptide for secretion are sufficient to interact with APP, which is in turn sufficient to inhibit the interaction of PS1 and APP.
the hydrophilicity of PS2NT and the presence of a leader peptide are sufficient to mediate its interaction with APP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interaction between PS1/2 and APP is not mediated through A beta but through the hydrophilic N-terminus of PS and a region encompassing A beta of APP.
the hydrophilicity of the amino terminus of the presenilins, in particular PS2, is sufficient for interaction with the A beta region of APP.
the interaction of presenilin and APP is a specific and biologically relevant event.
